warmup.text: In Chapter 24, Isaac spends a whole night awake while everyone else sleeps, and by morning Leader has made a dangerous vow. Your reading skill this week is summarizing. A good summary keeps only the events the story could not do without.

words.text: Two roots this week are about speaking. Voc, or voke, means voice or call. Dict means say. Then a year of spelling patterns, all in one sort. In the game, read each line and choose the word that fits the blank.

reading.text: Read Chapter 24 in your book. Watch what Leader vows, and how his own soldiers react. Then try the Read Like a Writer sentence about the wagon fire, and finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 24. Then your final writing piece of the unit begins. Today you only plan. Choose your strongest writing from the last five weeks, and decide what to keep, what to cut, and how to begin.

glossary.meaning: tell only the most important events, in a few words

miss.creative: create drops its last e before -ive: creat + ive.
miss.curiosity: curious drops its u before -ity: curios + ity.
miss.decision: decide drops its d-e before -sion: deci + sion.
miss.governor: Say gov-er-nor. The ending sounds like nur, but it is spelled o-r.
miss.mariner: Say mar-i-ner. The middle i makes a quiet uh sound.
miss.separate: Say sep-a-rate. The quiet middle is spelled a.

game.title: Raise Your Voice
game.sub: This week's word game · 3 lines today
game.look: Each line is something a person in Isaac's time could say. These lines are made up; they are not from the book. Read the whole line, then tap the word that fits the blank. Each line you finish sends a gold voice ring into the sky.

do: Read the whole line, blank and all.
Ask: voice and calling, or saying?
Tap the word that fits.
Tap Next line.
how.why: If you know voc, voke and dict, you can work out words you have never studied.

game.doneLine: Come back tomorrow for three more lines.

lines.before: When you do not know a word, look it up in the
lines.why: dict (say) + ionary: a book that says what words mean.

lines.before: She has the strongest voice in our choir. She is our best
lines.why: voc (voice) + al + ist: a person who uses their voice to sing.

lines.after: gave orders, and no one was allowed to speak against him.
lines.why: dict (say) + ator: a ruler whose word is the law.

art.title: The Magpie
art.alt: A painting of a snowy field and a wooden gate on a quiet morning, with a black and white bird sitting on the gate.
art.look: Claude Monet painted this snowy morning in France in the winter of 1868 to 1869. It is far from Isaac's road, but it feels like the morning in Chapter 24: the light comes slow and quiet, with no red streaks in the sky.

virtue.name: justice
virtue.title: Justice or not?
virtue.intro: You just read Chapter 24. Read each moment. Tap Justice or Not justice.

items.t: Roundman leaps to help Pointy Nose and packs the cut with snow.
items.why: He helps a hurt man when the leader will not. That is working to right a wrong.

items.t: Leader swings his shotgun at Pointy Nose for asking a question.
items.why: That is cruelty. Justice never means hurting someone to scare everyone else.

items.t: Jumper jumps into the cold river so Isaac and Joseph can save Naomi.
items.why: He took a risk to free someone who was held wrongly.

items.t: Leader says the girl and her family will pay.
items.why: He wants to get even. Getting even is not the same as making things right.
